content:
Following the release of the seventh developer betas of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and other upcoming Apple software updates, Apple is now rolling out the corresponding public betas. Here's what's new.

Apple rolls out new public betas

Apple earlier pushed out:

  • iOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24A5424a)
  • iPadOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24A5424a)
  • macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 7 (build number: 26A5421a)
  • tvOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24J5358a)
  • visionOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24M5359a)
  • watchOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24R5358a)

Apple is now rolling out the corresponding builds for its public beta testers — this marks the fifth round of public beta releases. So far, Apple has released new public betas for iOS 27, tvOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and HomePod 27.

Today's release doesn't include any major changes, as Apple is currently focused on bug fixes and stability improvements in preparation for an official launch expected in just a few weeks.

Additionally, Apple has released the second public release candidate (RC) of macOS Sequoia 15.8 (24H20), following the corresponding developer release candidate earlier this morning. The second release candidate of macOS Tahoe 26.7 (25G224) is also expected to drop soon. That build was also made available at the same time, 7:42 PM ET.

Across all of today's releases, the public beta build numbers are identical to their corresponding developer beta counterparts.

Enroll your device in the Apple Public Beta program

To enroll your device in the public beta program, head over to https://beta.apple.com and follow the steps for each respective device. Here's how to install the public beta on iPhone:

  • Visit the Apple Beta Software Program website and choose either "Enroll" or "Sign In."
  • Sign in with the same Apple Account you use on your iPhone, then accept the program terms and enroll your account.
  • Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  • Go to General > Software Update > Beta Updates.
  • Select "iOS 27 Public Beta."
  • Return to the Software Update screen and tap "Update Now" when the beta appears.

Apple recommends installing beta software on a secondary device. If you're using your primary iPhone, be sure to make a recent backup first.

Have you spotted any changes in today's beta? Let us know in the comments.
